description:
We are passionate about space, technology, gaming, and innovation.
For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are creating Mars Runner.
It is an interactive game where young astronauts explore Mars and collect resources.
Our goal is to make space science fun and educational for children.
summary: Mars Outpost is a free browser game for ages 7 to 12 that lets students run a Martian base for 5 sols. Players keep oxygen, power, water, food and radiation in balance. They walk around a 3D outpost, repair machines with spare parts, grow crops, clean dusty solar panels, shelter in the dome during radiation storms, and decide how to share limited power on a dashboard. A rover mini-game brings supplies back to the base. Every choice has a trade-off: more power for grow lights means less for life support. Messages from Earth arrive late, so players must decide on their own. After each mission, players see what happened, which choices they made and what to try next, along with real NASA science. It works on computers, tablets and phones.
details:
What it does: Mars Outpost teaches the engineering trade-offs of a real Mars base. Students survive 5 sols by balancing oxygen, power, water, food and radiation. Each fix costs something: spare parts cost power to make, crops cost water, and Power Saver mode cuts power use by 55% but raises oxygen use by 40%. Random events (dust storms, oxygen leaks, machine failures, radiation storms, lost communications) force quick decisions. Earth’s replies are delayed, as in real missions, so players learn autonomy. A rover mini-game (3-lane runner) gathers supplies for the base. Five training missions each teach one system. After every mission, a debrief shows what happened, the player’s decisions, what else to try, and the science behind it.

Benefits and impact: It turns hard concepts (life support, shielding, solar power, water recycling, growing food) into a game that a young learner can understand and enjoy. It runs in any modern browser, has touch and mouse controls, and has an Easy mode for younger players.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (3D), Web Audio API (all sound is generated by code), localStorage for saved progress. All art is made from code.

Creativity: Instead of a quiz, the learner runs the base and feels the trade-offs directly. Meters, storms and timers are simplified game calculations, not live NASA data. The game is not endorsed by NASA.

Factors considered: Age-appropriate language, short sessions, readable meters, accuracy of the facts, and honest labels for what is simplified.
